title: Sum of Even Numbers
directAnswer: Fold with a guard: add `x` to the total when `x % 2 == 0`. Empty or all-odd inputs give 0.

remember.takeaway: A fold plus an `if` filter handles 'sum of those that…' problems.
remember.formula: total=0; for x: if x%2==0: total+=x
whenToUse: Sum/aggregate of elements matching a predicate

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of only its even elements.
understanding: Accumulate, but add an element only when it is even.

approaches.name: Filtered accumulate
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
This is the accumulate fold with a **filter**: add an element to the running total only when it passes a test (here, `x % 2 == 0`). Seeding at 0 makes empty and all-odd inputs return 0 for free.

**Why the filter goes inside the loop.** You walk every element once, and the `if` decides whether it contributes. This 'fold + guard' shape generalises to 'sum of elements greater than k', 'sum of positives', etc. — only the predicate changes.

**Parity correctness.** Test `% 2 == 0`, not `% 2 == 1` for the complement, so negative evens (-2, -4) are summed correctly and negative odds are excluded.

**Overflow.** As with any array sum, accumulate into a `long` since the filtered total can still be large.

code.python:
def sum_even(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    return sum(x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0)

Seed at 0 so all-odd/empty inputs return 0.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one parity test and a conditional add per element.
pitfalls: Testing oddness with `% 2 == 1` and mishandling negatives.
Forgetting the filter and summing everything.

commonMistakes: Testing oddness with `% 2 == 1` and mishandling negatives.
Adding all elements and forgetting the filter.
patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Filtered fold. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
